collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE III: DEFENSE, RAIDS AND THE FALLEN (LCC-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
"If anyone comes to raid our homeland, we'll be ready." Isola's people are peaceful but no pushovers: stamping dances and war chants, watch fires and plans, raids fended off or not, prisoners and bargains, and how the village honors those who defended it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Raiders are stripping the far gardens at night: drive them off together, or let them take the food and stay safe.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) woke before dawn to the sound of voices in the far gardens: raiders, a dozen of them, pulling up the yams and filling sacks. (friend) is beside (subject.him/her) with a spear, ready to wake the warriors. But the raiders are armed too, and the village's people are still asleep. What should they do?

choices.label: Wake the Warriors and Drive Them Off

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The conch blows and the warriors come running with spears and torches, shouting the war chant. There is a short, ugly scuffle in the dark. The raiders flee to their canoes, leaving half the yams behind. (friend) has a long cut down (friend.his/her) arm that the healers stitch at dawn. The gardens are trampled, but the village held.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) holds (friend) back. They watch, silent and furious, while the raiders take what they can carry and paddle away. Nobody is hurt. The far gardens are bare. (friend) does not speak to (subject) for two days, then admits nobody would have been safe in the dark.
